=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:552-585 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_placeholder_recurrence_check` normalizes `HEAL_STALE_GREEN_RUNS` / `HEAL_STALE_MIN_AGE_HOURS` differently from the poller (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2988-3004). The judge accepts `^[1-9][0-9]{0,2}$` / `^[0-9]{1,4}$` with silent fallbacks to 5 and 24 and no cap. The poller accepts `^[0-9]{1,6}$`, caps GREEN_RUNS at 90 and warns.
  WHY: The judge and poller reach different close decisions on the same shared settings. A MIN_AGE of 10000 or more falls back to 24h, so the judge closes early. A GREEN_RUNS of 100..999 can never be met with the 100-run page at lines 584-585, so the hold never ends. A GREEN_RUNS of 1000 falls back to 5. The comment at .github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml:188, "The thresholds match the poller's heal stale close", is false. All four reviewers rated this MAJOR, mapped to high. claude-sonnet-5_5 raised the same point only as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:519-524 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `unblock_hold_patch_equivalent`, the target-branch fetch is capped at `--depth=300`, so `git cherry` cannot see a patch-equivalent commit older than 300 commits.
  WHY: A valid patch-equivalent commit outside the fetched history is not detected, so the `pr_on_branch` hold stays unmet until `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS`. This fails closed. Severity disagreement: gemini, minimax and luna rated it MAJOR (mapped to high); z-ai rated it NIT. claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected it, saying no realistic trigger was shown.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1259-1280 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_hold_close_no_recurrence` closes the issue before it marks the hold comment done. If the comment PATCH fails (it is not wrapped in gh_retry), the code only logs `outcome=warn reason=comment_failed`.
  WHY: Closed items are never scanned again (the scan covers open issues only, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26930-26933), so the issue stays closed with no explanation and a stale open `ai:unblock-wait:v1 hold=placeholder_retired` marker. A reopened item could be closed again at once. The poller's `_heal_stale_close_check` (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21270-21281) comments first and closes second. test_placeholder_hold_close_failure_keeps_the_hold_open locks in this behaviour. All reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1265-1267 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: When the close PATCH fails, `unblock_hold_close_no_recurrence` returns (the caller's `impossible)` branch is at about lines 2698-2703) without refreshing the open hold comment, unlike the unknown and unmet branches.
  WHY: The marker's updatedAt never moves, so the item is re-dispatched at the in-flight cadence instead of UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS. Each run repeats the runs-page read, the PR listing and the failed PATCH. `state["patched"] == []` in the test locks this in. All reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:616-625 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The linked-PR guard in `unblock_placeholder_recurrence_check` queries only open PRs with head `ai/issue-${ITEM}`. The poller's `_heal_stale_close_check` (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21237-21253) also uses the details map `linked_pr` and STALL_MANAGED_LINKED_PR_CACHE.
  WHY: A heal issue with an open "Fixes #<n>" PR on another branch is written as `null` (no linked PR), so the `open_pr` gate in heal_stale_decision (workflow_failure_heal.py:11254-11257) never fires, and the issue can be closed while the fix is still in review. Severity disagreement: luna rated it MAJOR (mapped to high); sonnet and minimax rated it NIT.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:546-602 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `workflow-failure-heal:source=` / `ai:workflow-heal-scope:v1 runs=` markers in the untrusted item.json choose the repo and numbers for authenticated `gh api` reads. These reads run before any check that the author is `UNBLOCK_LOGIN`; trust is enforced only later, in `_heal_stale_trusted` (workflow_failure_heal.py:11240-11241).
  WHY: A lookalike `ai:workflow-heal` issue can steer one authenticated read per run to an arbitrary `owner/repo#n`. This leaks repo-existence or access information and uses rate limit, though the decision still fails closed to unmet. All reviewers rated it NIT. claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected it (the label needs triage permission and the reads are GETs).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:524-526 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In `unblock_hold_patch_equivalent`, the check `git cherry "refs/remotes/origin/${branch}" "${sha}" "${sha}^"` combined with `grep -qv '^- '` depends on how `<limit>` is interpreted. It may return empty output, or trip on `+` lines from intermediate ancestors on a multi-commit PR. The test fixture `_patch_equivalence_remote` (tests/test_unblock_judge.py:4209-4240) covers only a one-commit history.
  WHY: On a real multi-commit PR, the `pr_on_branch` hold could stay unmet until `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS`. Rated MAJOR (mapped to high). claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash both explicitly rejected this class of claim: the three-argument form limits the range to `sha^..sha`, a single commit.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:11125-11131 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `heal_stale_target` now reports `source_kind="pr"` and `source_number=N`, and the judge treats PR-sourced heals as close-eligible. The poller still skips them with `not_run_sourced` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21173-21175).
  WHY: The two surfaces disagree on whether PR-sourced heals are close-eligible. After a judge close, the next orchestrator tick may file a re-issue against the same source. The divergence is intentional per the plan, but the two surfaces are not coordinated.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:491-493 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_hold_git_fetch` sets `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="http.https://github.com/.extraheader"`, which scopes the auth header to github.com only.
  WHY: On GHES (`GITHUB_SERVER_URL` set to another host), the fetch goes out unauthenticated and fails silently, so every `pr_on_branch` hold stays unmet. claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same point as hardening only.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:552-555 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Invalid threshold values fall back silently to `green_runs=5` / `min_age=24` with no `::warning::`, unlike the poller (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2989-2992).
  WHY: An operator typo such as `HEAL_STALE_GREEN_RUNS=five` is hidden on every run, which violates the "match the poller" contract stated in the yml comment at line 188.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:582-595 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The judge reads `actions/workflows/<wf>/runs` for every held heal item. unblock_judge.yml does not forward `HEAL_STALE_RUNS_CACHE_JSON` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3007), so the cache lookup at line 582 is always empty.
  WHY: This adds one fresh runs-page API read per held heal per judge run, multiplied across held heals on the same workflow or branch.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:540-630 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `UNBLOCK_PLACEHOLDER_RECURRENCE_CHECK_ENABLED` is true, the path adds four authenticated gh api reads plus one Python CLI call per held heal item. It has no pre-read author check and no source_repo allowlist. This surface is not declared in the yml comment or the README row.
  WHY: Operators who enable the switch get a larger implicit API surface than the switch comment implies, and the effective gate is the post-hoc `_heal_stale_trusted`.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "README.md edits are append-only and use existing <!-- anchor:NAME --> anchors. Do not reflow unrelated content." (Linked issue #9967, Files section.)
  expected_change_site: README.md, anchored table under <!-- anchor:required-variables-table --> (README.md:2681)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The README hunk `@@ -135,6 +135,8 @@` (lines 135-142, rows at lines 138-139) inserts `UNBLOCK_HOLD_PATCH_EQUIVALENCE_ENABLED` and `UNBLOCK_PLACEHOLDER_RECURRENCE_CHECK_ENABLED` mid-table, between `UNBLOCK_NOTHING_TO_IMPLEMENT_CLOSE_ENABLED` and `UNBLOCK_TRIAGE_NOTHING_TO_IMPLEMENT_GATE_ENABLED`, in the unblock_judge variables table (lines 97-144). Nothing is added at the required-variables-table anchor. The file has only three anchors (README.md:200 area, :2681, :3527), and none covers this table. Mitigation noted by minimax and z-ai: the rows follow the precedent of the surrounding UNBLOCK_* rows, and no unrelated content was reflowed. claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this gap.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_hold_close_no_recurrence (about lines 1259-1280) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The code closes the issue via `gh api -X PATCH ... state=closed` before `unblock_patch_comment` (which is not wrapped in gh_retry). If the comment fails, the issue is closed with no reason, the "Waiting for ..." hold comment and the open `ai:unblock-wait:v1` marker remain, and no Telegram DEBUG notice is sent, unlike `_heal_stale_close_check` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 21270-21281, 21284).
  WHY: Closed items are not scanned again. If the issue is reopened, the open placeholder_retired hold makes the judge close it again at once. Fix: write the done-marker comment first and close only on success, or retry with gh_retry.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_placeholder_recurrence_check, linked-PR block (`pulls?state=open&head=${owner}:ai/issue-${ITEM}&per_page=1`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Only an open `ai/issue-<n>` PR counts as linked. The poller also uses the details map `linked_pr` and STALL_MANAGED_LINKED_PR_CACHE (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21237-21253). The judge writes `null`, which heal_stale_decision (workflow_failure_heal.py:11254-11257) reads as "no linked PR".
  WHY: A heal with an open "Fixes #<n>" PR on another branch passes the open_pr gate and can be closed while the fix is still in review. Impact is limited because the failure is in fact green.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_hold_close_no_recurrence close_failed path; caller `impossible)` branch (about lines 2698-2703) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A failed close returns without refreshing the open hold comment, unlike the unknown and unmet branches (lines 2673-2695). test_placeholder_hold_close_failure_keeps_the_hold_open asserts `state["patched"] == []`.
  WHY: On a persistent failure (for example a 403), updatedAt never moves, so the item is re-dispatched at the in-flight cadence instead of the retry cadence and repeats its reads and the failed PATCH. Fix: fall through to the unmet refresh, or patch a "Last checked" line.
- Pass-1 findings checked and rejected: git cherry lists all of upstream..sha (z-ai, MAJOR; the three-argument form walks only `sha`, and the comment at lines 505-506 is accurate); depth 300 hides older equivalen
